item.title: [KAN-18] US-01 Verify customer identity before portal access
item.description:
User story: As a delinquent customer, I want to verify my identity using core account attributes, so that my confidential financial details remain protected.

Business value: Prevents unauthorised data disclosure and complies with UK banking data protection standards while enabling self-service.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Account details and balances remain completely hidden until all identity verification criteria succeed
  • Verification matches customer-entered DOB, postal code, and account reference against legacy records
  • Failed attempts increment an unverified counter and present a clear retry prompt

Dependencies: None

Backlog priority: Highest - A portal will be unusable if not accessed via secure login, as the data security needs are strict. The first stage in using the portal for customers, so there are a lot of later dependencies.
item.summary: US-01 Verify customer identity before portal access

item.title: [KAN-19] US-02 Enforce verification attempt limit and lockout referral
item.description:
User story: As a Data Security manager, I want the system to lock out a session after 3 consecutive failed verification attempts, so that brute-force credential stuffing is blocked.

Business value: Protects bank systems from automated attacks and prevents customer distress by redirecting stuck users to representatives.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Exactly 3 consecutive verification failures lock the customer reference for self-service for 24 hours
  • Upon the 3rd failure, the customer is shown a secure screen to provide contact/account details, which get added to the representative queue.
  • System logs the lockout event with timestamp, IP hash, and failure reason code to portal metadata

Dependencies: US-01

Backlog priority: Medium - The specific number of attempts before lockout is arbitrary. It is important for data security reasons but has little impact on operational efficiency or ROI generation.

Notes: Aligns with Gareth’s requirement to prevent customer circular loops while safeguarding account access.
item.summary: US-02 Enforce verification attempt limit and lockout referral

item.title: [KAN-20] US-03 Enable representative security verification and credential reset
item.description:
User story: As a collections representative, I want to authenticate a customer who failed online verification and reset their portal credentials, so that legitimate customers can regain self-service access and I don’t have to complete the full process with them.

Business value: Eliminates manual dead-ends, empowering representatives to resolve authentication blockers. Reroutes some failed portal interactions back to the portal, ensuring the representative load is still reduced.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Representatives know the customer was referred due to failed login and are presented with security questions and answers.
  • Representative can trigger a one-click credential unlock/reset upon successful telephony challenge
  • Unlock action generates an auditable event record linking representative ID to the customer record

Dependencies: US-02

Backlog priority: High - Where security is a major concern, we want the actual required agent intervention to be minimal, to avoid wasting agent time and impacting the ROI generated by agent time-savings.

Notes: Critical ADKAR capability item: representative teams must be trained to reset access rather than taking over simple queries manually.
item.summary: US-03 Enable representative security verification and credential reset

item.title: [KAN-21] US-04 Route customer back to portal following representative reset
item.description:
User story: As a customer whose credentials were reset by a representative, I want the option to restart my session online, so that I can self-resolve without staying on the telephone.

Business value: Maximises portal adoption and frees up representative capacity immediately after clearing authentication roadblocks.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Once a representative resets credentials, the system issues an SMS/email magic re-entry link valid for 15 minutes
  • Customer accessing the link is brought directly to a refreshed verification screen with zeroed attempt count
  • If the customer declines portal restart, the representative is prompted to proceed with standard case handling

Dependencies: US-03

Backlog priority: High - Similarly to US-03, this step is vital to maintain the high agent time savings that generate the project’s financial ROI.

Notes: Requires access to communication history in full scale implementation.
item.summary: US-04 Route customer back to portal following representative reset

item.title: [KAN-22] US-05 Display real-time overdue balance and delinquency status
item.description:
User story: As a verified delinquent customer, I want to view my current overdue balance, total balance, and days in arrears, so that I understand my debt position clearly.

Business value: Deflects routine balance inquiries (accounting for 12.49% of all collections contacts) to automated self-service.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Verified customer dashboard displays exact overdue amount, current balance, and arrears status fetched from legacy storage
  • All necessary values are displayed with the timestamp of the last system update
  • If the legacy database is unreachable, a graceful degradation screen displays with an apology and retry option

Dependencies: US-01, Legacy database

Backlog priority: High - Preventing recontact and allowing customers instant access to their information will lead to large agent time savings. This information is also needed to build the payment planning steps from.

Notes: Read-only connection to legacy collections database. Caching layer recommended.
item.summary: US-05 Display real-time overdue balance and delinquency status

item.title: [KAN-23] US-06 Display context-sensitive eligible next actions
item.description:
User story: As a verified customer, I want to see only the repayment actions I am eligible to take, so that I do not attempt unsupported resolution paths.

Business value: Eliminates customer confusion, curtails drop-offs, and ensures customers only proceed along policy-approved pathways.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Dashboard dynamically presents available pathways (Eligible Repayment Plans, Vulnerability Self-Report) based on account status
  • Ineligible actions are suppressed from view rather than disabled without explanation
  • Customer action selection is recorded as an interaction event in portal metadata

Dependencies: US-05

Backlog priority: High - Payment plan selection was identified as the highest ROI automation opportunity

Notes: Requires algorithmic elimination of ineligible plans for standard cases.
item.summary: US-06 Display context-sensitive eligible next actions

item.title: [KAN-24] US-07 Implement session inactivity warning and safe pause
item.description:
User story: As the delivery team, I want the portal to warn the user and safely pause after 3 minutes of inactivity, so that unattended sessions do not leak financial data.

Business value: Safeguards sensitive debt data in shared environments and enables automated queue tracking for abandoned sessions.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Modal countdown warning appears after 2 minutes of user inactivity, giving 60 seconds to extend
  • Expiration at 3 minutes terminates the authenticated session, clears sensitive DOM data, and displays a timeout screen
  • System records session timeout event, logs last visited screen, and flags case in metadata

Dependencies: US-01

Backlog priority: Medium - Data security and privacy needs are important, but this isn't integral to any later stages and doesn’t directly improve financial viability of the project.

Notes: Directly corresponds to BPMN Subprocess (Session Timeout Check).
item.summary: US-07 Implement session inactivity warning and safe pause

item.title: [KAN-25] US-08 Evaluate automated payment plan eligibility rules
item.description:
User story: As the operations manager, I want the system to evaluate customer account attributes against policy criteria, so that only manageable, policy-compliant payment plans are offered.

Business value: Mitigates default risk by ensuring self-serve plans strictly comply with credit risk policy.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Eligibility evaluation executes automatically upon customer selecting repayment plan pathway
  • System assesses arrears tier, account age, and active disputes, categorising the account as Eligible or Unsupported, for each plan.
  • Cases with no eligible plans are not routed to the self-serve platform.

Dependencies: US-06, Policy criteria specified by internal team

Backlog priority: High - Required for compliance, customer satisfaction, and reducing errors resulting in agent re-assessment.
item.summary: US-08 Evaluate automated payment plan eligibility rules

item.title: [KAN-26] US-09 Present payment plan options with schedule breakdowns
item.description:
User story: As an eligible customer, I want to review structured payment plan options with instalment amounts, so that I can select a sustainable repayment path.

Business value: Enables self-service debt restructuring, replacing manual calculations previously conducted by telephone representatives.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Screen presents eligible instalment options detailing frequency (weekly/monthly), instalment amount, and end date
  • Total repayable under each option explicitly breaks down arrears, interest, fees, and penalties.

Dependencies: US-08

Backlog priority: High - Required for customers to provide payment confirmations.
item.summary: US-09 Present payment plan options with schedule breakdowns

item.title: [KAN-27] US-10 Confirm selected payment plan and generate payment agreement
item.description:
User story: As an eligible customer, I want to confirm my chosen plan and view legal agreement terms, so that I have formal clarity on my commitment.

Business value: Secures customer commitment and provides clear audit-ready evidentiary agreement required by compliance.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Selection screen displays all necessary payment plan information.
  • Customer must actively tick statutory acknowledgment before Confirm Agreement button activates.
  • Confirmation screen provides downloadable PDF summary and unique agreement reference code.
  • Confirmation logs customer details to internal systems.

Dependencies: US-09

Backlog priority: High - Required for promise-to-pay capture
item.summary: US-10 Confirm selected payment plan and generate payment agreement

item.title: [KAN-28] US-11 Capture digital promise to pay with amount and commitment date
item.description:
User story: As a customer unable to pay the full debt immediately, I want to submit a Promise to Pay for my payment plan, so that I avoid escalation calls.

Business value: Automates routine promise-to-pay capture (accounting for 12.08% of sample interactions), directly reducing representative call volume.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Form validates that promised amount meets minimum threshold percentage of overdue balance
  • Successful submission displays formal PTP receipt
  • Successful submission pauses outbound collections contact until commitment date

Dependencies: US-05, US-06

Backlog priority: Highest - Second highest ROI opportunity
item.summary: US-11 Capture digital promise to pay with amount and commitment date

item.title: [KAN-29] US-12 Write payment commitments and schedules back to legacy database
item.description:
User story: As the leader of the representative team, I want to write confirmed PTPs and plans into the legacy collections database, so that records remain synchronised and my team don’t double hand cases.

Business value: Eliminates manual rekeying by representatives and ensures follow-up automation operates off single-source-of-truth records.

Acceptance criteria:

  • System executes transactional write of PTP/plan details (amount, due date, terms) to legacy database within 5 seconds
  • Write confirms success via acknowledgment token before releasing confirmation to customer
  • Failed writes trigger automated retry (up to 3 times) before queuing a case for manual fallback

Dependencies: US-10, US-11

Backlog priority: High - required to prevent agent double-handling of cases and to ensure agent time savings are realised.

Notes: Requires interaction with the legacy database and should be designed to transition if internal data structures are improved at a later date.
item.summary: US-12 Write payment commitments and schedules back to legacy database

item.title: [KAN-30] US-13 Route simple cases to the self-serve platform, and complex cases to the representative queue, with a clear prioritisation structure
item.description:
User story: As the head of collections operations, I want clear routing rules for incoming cases, so that my representatives can work on the highest-priority cases.

Business value: Removes customer interactions from the portal that cannot be solved there due to complexity, ensuring the validity of portal performance data. Prevents representatives from spending undue time on simplistic cases

Acceptance criteria:

  • Accounts with no viable payment plans that meet high-risk criteria, or are at the final stage before escalation, are routed to agents, not the platform.
  • Routing payload contains reason code (e.g., BALANCE_EXCEEDS_LIMIT, PLAN_REJECTED)
  • Queue priority is assigned dynamically based on delinquency severity, case pending time, and balance risk tier

Dependencies: US-08, US-09

Backlog priority: Medium - The routing decisions were a ‘should’ for project scope, as they do not form a direct part of the self-service portal. Having said that, they are key to removing traffic from agent workflows.

Notes: Solves Gareth Evans major concern: ensuring complex cases do not fall between channel cracks.
item.summary: US-13 Route simple cases to the self-serve platform, and complex cases to the representative queue, with a clear prioritisation structure

item.title: [KAN-31] US-14 Support self-reported financial vulnerability and trigger collections pause
item.description:
User story: As a customer experiencing financial vulnerability, I want to notify the bank online, so that collections activities are halted while specialist care is arranged.

Business value: Guarantees regulatory compliance with FCA vulnerability guidance, preventing inappropriate automated enforcement on vulnerable customers.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Customer selecting Report Financial Vulnerability is presented with a supportive, non-intimidating self-declaration screen
  • Submission immediately applies a statutory collections hold on the account across all systems
  • Case is routed directly to the manual handling queue with customer-entered context attached

Dependencies: US-06

Backlog priority: Medium - Regulatory requirement, but at the specified complexity it is not a prerequisite for other tasks, and can increase agent workload if misused.

Notes: Directly implements BPMN Subprocess (Self-Report Financial Vulnerability). Non-negotiable compliance requirement.
item.summary: US-14 Support self-reported financial vulnerability and trigger collections pause

item.title: [KAN-32] US-15 Process customer request for representative contact
item.description:
User story: As a customer preferring human support, I want to request a representative contact from the portal, so that I can discuss my account without waiting on hold.

Business value: Reduces customer frustration, mitigates inbound phone surges, and organizes representative outbound call queues.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Form captures preferred callback telephone number, best contact window (Morning/Afternoon), and brief topic category
  • System validates contact number format and creates outbound task in representative queue
  • Confirmation screen provides estimated callback SLA and reference number

Dependencies: US-06

Backlog priority: Low - As opposed to this, simply not removing platformed cases from the queue would default to this option, though with a less-smooth process for customers.
item.summary: US-15 Process customer request for representative contact

item.title: [KAN-34] US-17 Display customer portal interaction history in representative console
item.description:
User story: As a collections representative, I want to view a timeline of customer portal activity, so that I never ask customers to repeat information already provided.

Business value: Drastically reduces call handling times and eliminates representative frustration, driving internal ADKAR desire and adoption.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Case view console renders chronological timeline of portal interactions (screens viewed, failed attempts, plans inspected, details entered)
  • Timeline clearly marks exact reason for channel transition or routing failure
  • Interaction history loads concurrently with case opening, adding zero additional clicks or screen switches

Dependencies: US-01, US-11, US-13

Backlog priority: High - Positive ROI change that reduces wasted time for agents, increases customer satisfaction, and increases data visibility for audit.

Notes: Directly satisfies Gareth Evans' requirement: eliminates repetitive context-gathering by representative staff.
item.summary: US-17 Display customer portal interaction history in representative console

item.title: [KAN-35] US-18 Record immutable timestamped audit log of key customer actions
item.description:
User story: As the compliance officer, I want tamper-evident logs of customer consent, declarations, and payment submissions, so that the bank can evidence regulatory compliance.

Business value: Satisfies evidentiary standards, insulating the bank from legal challenges regarding disputed debt arrangements.

Acceptance criteria:

  • System records UTC timestamp, customer ID, IP address, action type, and payload hash for all verifications and agreements
  • Audit logs are written to append-only, tamper-evident storage inaccessible to manual editing
  • Audit query interface allows compliance officers to extract full customer journey logs by account reference

Dependencies: US-01, US-10, US-11

Backlog priority: High - the main basis for improved auditability in the self-serve platform as opposed to existing internal messy processes. Reduces the latter complexity of reconciliation processes, saving manager time.

Notes: Core prerequisite for Daniel Okoye’s sign-off on the legal validity of digital arrangements.
item.summary: US-18 Record immutable timestamped audit log of key customer actions

item.title: [KAN-37] US-20 Capture journey funnel completion, drop-off, and routing telemetry
item.description:
User story: As the product manager, I want granular event tracking across every portal step, so that I can identify journey drop-off, assess the effectiveness of the portal, and optimize conversion.

Business value: Provides empirical proof of portal usability and highlights bottleneck steps requiring UX revision or policy refinement.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Telemetry framework captures anonymised events on every step transition (Screen View, Step Complete, Abandon, Error)
  • System differentiates between successful self-service completion, voluntary drop-off, and automated representative routing
  • Telemetry data aggregates in a real-time reporting datastore without impacting front-end responsiveness

Dependencies: US-01, US-05, US-10

Backlog priority: High - Required to assess financial success of project integration
item.summary: US-20 Capture journey funnel completion, drop-off, and routing telemetry

item.title: [KAN-38] US-21 Generate operational workload deflection and capacity shift report
item.description:
User story: As the Head of Collections Operations, I want weekly reports on call deflection and representative time saved, so that I can prove the 12-month ROI case.

Business value: Proves the 12-month payback hypothesis to Daniel Okoye and provides management visibility into operational capacity shift.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Report compares weekly portal-resolved cases against baseline representative call handling hours (18.5 mins/call)
  • Output quantifies hours of representative time freed up across balance checks and routine PTPs
  • Dashboard displays trend charts of self-service resolution rate vs. routed exceptions

Dependencies: US-20

Backlog priority: Low - Automating the creation of the report is not as important as ensuring the data is tracked.

Notes: Key deliverable for Daniel Okoye senior leadership briefing and Gareth Evans resource planning.
item.summary: US-21 Generate operational workload deflection and capacity shift report
